Compared with the two relatively closed systems in Europe, the exchange between Great and Little traditions was smoother in imperial China, and in the mixing and communication between the two traditions in the early imperial period, the Han Confucian scholars, who served as “benevolent officials”, played an irreplaceable role.

improve and make it more academic: Philosophically, the Han Confucians “contributed nothing new”, but they did play a role in “changing traditions and customs”, making the concept of filial piety and fraternal duty take root in the hearts of the people. The Han Confucians replaced the delicate philosophical arguments of the Pre-Qin Confucianism with the popular concepts of Yin, Yang and Five Elements. The beliefs in popular culture were accepted by Confucianism, and the basic teachings of Confucianism thus broke through the barriers of elite culture and were well-received by the general public. Confucius said, “Instead of talking about truths with mere words, I would like to examine concrete examples so as to explain my views on human affairs profoundly and clearly.” Confucianism in the Han mainly applied to the domain of human morality and daily life, which belongs to the sphere of what is known as culture and society today. Politics in the Han was not determined solely by Confucianism. Confucianization was a subtle process, relying more on the general public than the imperial court and more on customs than institutions. As “officials close to the civilian”, benevolent officials played a more important role than ministers and scripture teachers.

improve and make it more academic: The so-called great-family politics refers to the sharing of political power between eminent gentry families and the emperor. The typical example is the so-called fact that “The families of Wang and (Si) Ma share the power”. In the Eastern Jin, the emperor not fulfilling his duties, eminent families seizing the power, and the emergence of refugees all contributed to the maintenance of great-family politics. Great-family politics is a “perversion of imperial politics”, and there are three special conditions for its formation: first, a mature and influential social class (shizu,士族 influential and privileged families of scholar-officials); second, a royal family that lost its authority and still had a certain appeal; third, sharp ethnic contradictions. However, the great-family politics was both temporary and transitional: firstly, it was not easy for the expatriate eminent families from the north to gain a foothold to the east of the Yangtze River in the south, and it was even more difficult for them to take root; secondly, the gentry families only held command over the army, but never fought in the battlefield themselves, and thus could not substantively “manipulate the military power” and became increasingly weak; thirdly, the talent of the gentry clans dwindled, probably due to the degradation of the race caused by limited intermarriage. The emperors of the Southern Dynasties restored their authority, but the great families maintained their social, political, and “refined and graceful” edges. The three elements of Chinese culture (national consciousness, Confucianism, and the imperial examination system) came to “full blossom” in the Song Dynasty. %% simulating a bouncing ball
% This script simulates a ball dropped or thrown in a vertical direction
% under constant gravitational acceleration. The ball will hit the floor
% and it will bounce a multiple number of times based on the coefficient
% of restitution given by epsilon. We have just before/after a collision.
% epsilon = |just after velocity| divided by |just before velocity|
%
% INPUT
% yo = initial height of ball
% vyo = initial velocity of ball in the y-direction
% dt = time resolution
% tMax = total time of the process
% epsilon = coefficient of restitution
%
% PROCESS
% solve differential equation using Euler’s method
% use crude approximation to determine when ball hits floor
%
% OUTPUT
% height versus time graph
% velocity versus time graph
clear all % never not do this
%% set initial condition
to = 0; % initial time on clock (seconds)
yo = 2.5; % meters (m)
vyo = 5; % velocity --> meters/second (m/s)
dt = 0.001; % time resolution --> seconds (s)
tMax = 20; % maximum time range --> (s)
epsilon = 0.7; % coefficient of restitution (unitless)
%% set constants
ay = -9.8; % acceleratin due to gravity m/s^2
%% solve differential equation using Euler’s method
%% Create interpolation data for velocity versus height
heights = [0, 2.5]; % heights at which velocity is known (m)
velocities = [0, vyo]; % velocities at corresponding heights (m/s)
v_interpolation = @(h) interp1(heights, velocities, h); % interpolation function

%% solve differential equation using Euler’s method
tArray = to; % time range as an array (s)
y = yo; % preallocate the y array (height) (m)
vy = vyo; % preallocate the vy array (height) (m)

% ------------------------------- calculate position as a function of time
while tArray(end) < (to+tMax)
% ----------------------------------------------------------- detect floor
t = tArray(end);
vy_next = vy(end) + ay*dt;
y_next = y(end) + vy(end)dt;

if (y_next <= 0) % => hit the floor with dt time resolution
% Linear interpolation for velocity just before collision at y = 0
vy_collision = v_interpolation(y_next);

% Update the velocity and height after collision
vy_next = - vy_collisionepsilon;
y_next = 0;

% Append the interpolated velocities and heights to the arrays
tArray = [tArray, t+dt/2, t+dt];
vy = [vy, vy_collision, vy_next];
y = [y, 0, 0];
else
% Append the next velocity and height to the arrays
tArray = [tArray, t+dt];
vy = [vy, vy_next];
y = [y, y_next];
end
end

%% plot results
figure(1);
clf;
plot(tArray,y,‘b’,‘lineWidth’,1.8);
xlabel(‘time (seconds)’);
ylabel(‘height (meters)’);

figure(2);
plot(tArray,vy,‘b’,‘lineWidth’,1.8);
xlabel(‘time (seconds)’);
ylabel(‘velocity (meters)’);

improve and make it more academic: In the Qing Dynasty, special examinations on imperial order included categories such as “broad learning and extensive words” in the 17th year of Emperor Kangxi (AD 1678) and the first year of Emperor Qianlong (AD 1736), and “statecraft” in the 22nd year of the Guangxu Emperor in1896.

improve and make it more academic: High-ranking officials would recommend to the emperor their talented or meritorious subordinates for promotion, . It made up for the demerit of the assessment system, and thus took part of the power of the Ministry of Personnel. In the Han Dynasty, this recommendation and appointment process was named biju (辟举), where the Three Dukes, commanderies and counties had the power to recommend talents and place them on probation for their subordinate offices , and then appointed or promoted them upon vacancy in order based on records of the talents’ conduct and performance, with some even promoted to high-ranking posts of 2000 bushels. In the Northern Qi, the power of high officials to recommend their own subordinates was taken away by the Ministry of Personnel.

improve and make it more academic:  The practice of guaranteed recommendation later flourished in the Ming and Qing Dynasties. It began in the Ming in the 17th year of the Hongwu era (AD 1384) when court officials were ordered to recommend capable and incorrupt subordinates, and in the Yongle era of the Ming, the collective punishment was implemented to hold recommenders responsible for the malpractice of the recommended. The progress of time saw rampant corruption with the guaranteed recommendation system so that some officials gave underhand favors to their fellow townsmen, relatives, or subordinates, while other officials could not be promoted for many years without proper recommenders. The guaranteed recommendation, introduced in the middle of the Qing when it was plagued by both internal disturbance and foreign aggression, sustained till the fall of the empire. At that time, “it was possible to save the dynasty from collapse with force”, “virtuous heroes could not be selected through imperial examinations”, and “it was common for subordinates and private secretaries to squeeze into the powerful and influential ranks simply due to their superiors’ word of recommendation”. For example, when Zeng Guofan (statesman and military general of the late Qing) was suppressing the Taiping Rebellion, there were abundant talents among his private secretaries. Zuo Zongtang, Li Hongzhang, Peng Yuli, etc. were among those who rose to high positions through the recommendation of Zeng.

improve and make it more academic:  
In the Han Dynasty, the issues of regional and ethnic equality were already taken into account in the allocation of quota for the recommendation of filial and incorrupt talents. In the Eastern Han, the quotas were distributed according to the population of each commandery, “the emperor regarded it as unfair that the quotas were two for both big commanderies with a population between 500-600 thousand, and small commanderies with a population around 200 thousand and barbarians. Therefore, the emperor handed it down to high-ranking ministers for discussion.” After the discussion, the quota system was modified as follows: “The population sizes of those commanderies and princedoms determines the quota of filial and incorrupt talents, with one for a 200,000 population, two for 600,000, four for 800, 000, five for one million, and six for 1.2 million. For commanderies with a population smaller than 200 thousand, the quota is one every two years while for commanderies with a population smaller than 100 thousand, one every three years” (quotes from Biography of Ding Hong in Book of the Later Han). At the same time, preferential treatment was given to the sparsely populated border areas where the Han and ethnic minorities were mixed. For instance, “the Provinces of Youzhou, Bingzhou, and Liangzhou are sparsely populated, but border corvée labor is very heavy. Good officials have limited opportunities for advancement. However, the appeasement and reception of the barbarian depends on suitable officials. Now, it is ordered that the quota of recommendation of filial and incorrupt talents for remote border commanderies with a population of over 100 thousand was one per year; with a population smaller than 100 thousand, one every two years; and with a population smaller than 50 thousand, one every three years” (quotes from Annal of Emperor Xiaohe in Book of the Later Han).

improve and make it more academic:  
In the Song Dynasty, a regional quota system was adopted for provincial graduates. However, there was no regional quota restriction for palace graduates, and the practice of “free distribution among regions” was implemented. When imperial examinations were launched in the Yuan, the quota system was installed for the metropolitan examinations, and the places established by the official quota were equally distributed among Mongols, Semu, Han Chinese, and Southerners. Southerners then lived in regions that were known as Jiangsu, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hubei, and Henan in the Southern Song. Consequently, the quotas for Han Chinese and Southerners, who accounted for the majority of the population, were relatively small, and the discrimination against Southerners was particularly obvious. Different from the Song, the regional quota system in the Yuan was mainly based on geopolitics, paying special attention to the balanced distribution of political power. In effect, “the quota is allocated more based on class or ethnicity than region” (Lin, 2005).

The fly ash used in this study was collected from the dust collector of a municipal waste incineration plant. The fly ash was analyzed for its ash composition and ash fusion characteristics. X-ray fluorescence spectroscopy (XRF) was employed to analyze the ash composition of the waste incineration fly ash. The ash fusion characteristics were determined according to the standard GB/T 219-2008 “Test Method for Fusibility of Coal Ash” under oxidizing atmosphere. The results are presented in Table 1. From Table 1, it can be observed that the main components of the waste incineration fly ash are CaO, Cl, Na2O, K2O, and SiO2. The highest content is attributed to Ca, which is primarily due to the addition of a large amount of lime during the flue gas purification process in the waste incineration plant, resulting in a high CaO content in the fly ash. The Cl content is also high, mainly because municipal solid waste contains chloride-containing substances such as plastics and kitchen waste, which release a significant amount of Cl upon incineration. During the flue gas treatment process, Cl tends to accumulate in the fly ash particles. Additionally, the content of SiO2 (2.82%) and Al2O3 (0.88%) in the waste incineration fly ash is relatively low.

Background: The excessive correction of acute hypernatremia is not known to be harmful. This study aimed to evaluate
whether a reduction rate of serum sodium (RRSeNa) 4 1 mEq/L/hour in acute severe hypernatremia is an independent risk
factor for mortality in critically ill patients undergoing continuous venovenous hemofiltration (CV VH) treatment.
Materials and Methods: For this retrospective study, we reviewed records of 75 critically ill patients undergoing CV VH
treatment for acute severe hypernatremia between March 2011 and March 2015.
Results: The 28-day mortality rate of all patients was 61.3%. In multivariate Cox regression analyses, a reduction rate of serum
sodium (RRSeNa) 4 1 mEq/L/hour (hazard ratio ¼ 1.89; 95% CI: 1.03-3.47; P ¼ 0.04), Acute Physiology and Chronic Health
Evaluation II score and vasopressor dependency (yes or no) had a statistically significantly effect on mortality. Once we excluded
patients with an RRSeNa r 0.5 mEq/L/hour, only RRSeNa 4 1 mEq/L/hour (hazard ratio ¼ 2.611; 95% CI: 1.228-5.550;
P ¼ 0.013) and vasopressor dependency had a statistically significant influence on mortality in multivariate regression.
Conclusions: In addition to the Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II score and vasopressor dependency, the
excessive correction of acute severe hypernatremia was possibly associated with mortality in critically ill patients undergoing
CV VH treatment. The optimal reduction rate of acute hypernatremia should be extensively studied in critically ill patients.
Key Indexing Terms: Hypernatremia; Continuous venovenous hemofiltration; Reduction rate of serum sodium; Mortality.

“iPager isn’t real, but the problems that Apple causes by using SMS are,” said Google in the video description on YouTube. “Let’s make texting better for everyone and help Apple #GetTheMessage and upgrade to RCS.”
RCS offers several improvements to messaging, including end-to-end encryption, read receipts, and the ability to share high-resolution photos and videos. iMessage offers similar features but only for messages sent between other iMessage users, resulting in Android users being seen as green message bubble nuisances in group messages — a real issue in countries like the US where more than half the population is using an iPhone.

Carriers and phone manufacturers like Samsung have already adopted RCS technology, but Apple’s commitment to its own iMessage standard has drawn Google’s ire for some time. In January last year, Google SVP Hiroshi Lockheimer criticized Apple for “holding back the user experience” for customers. Apple hasn’t budged its stance despite Google’s lighthearted bullying — last year at the Code Conference, Tim Cook said anyone frustrated by their green message bubbles should just buy an iPhone.

Court documents from Apple’s legal dispute with Epic Games in 2021 revealed that the iPhone maker sees its iMessage platform as a key service for locking customers into its ecosystem and that it believes moving iMessage to Android would “hurt us more than help.” So providing Android users with an iMessage-like experience by adopting RCS is presumably low on Apple’s priorities.

In Shiraz, his uncle sent him to a maktab primary school, where he remained for six or seven years.[10] In contrast to the formal, orthodox theology which dominated the school curriculum of the time, which included the study of jurisprudence and Arabic grammar, the Báb from a young age felt inclined towards unconventional subjects like mathematics and calligraphy, which were little studied. The Bab's preoccupation with spirituality, creativity and imagination also angered his teachers and was not tolerated in the atmosphere of the 19th-century Persian school system.[11] This led the Báb to become disillusioned with the education system, he later instructs adults to treat children with dignity, to allow children to have toys and engage in play[12] and to never show anger or harshness to their students.[13]

Given these conditions, the factory system was unattractive to the traditional manufacturing workforce accustomed to fluid working schedules, full control over work, self-employment, ability to self-consume the goods they produced, ownership of their own small businesses, pride and passion in work, given credit for work, relatively well-ventilated and lit workshops and good middle-class pay and so Samuel Slater, Francis Cabot Lowell and other mill owners had to rely on displaced New England farmers, young New England farm girls and children who had little to no other viable choices for work

These same unattractive conditions are also among the reasons Samuel Slater and other mill owners chose Pawtucket as their mill location which was a more rural community than the urban centers of New England that were home to a considerable population of skilled artisans

Then in 1814, a wealthy Boston merchant named Francis Cabot Lowell founded the Boston Manufacturing Company with a group of investors named The Boston Associates, It built the first vertically integrated cotton mill that integrated spinning, weaving, dyeing, and cutting all under one building with Paul Moody's first American power loom and Moody's system of power transmission using a series of leather belts and pulleys powered by water turbines, that would prove much more efficient than the shaft and gear system then in use, an improvement over Slater's mills

The use of mill girls nonetheless did represent the first time that an improvement to the factory labor landscape was made since Slater's first 1793 Slater Mill which used child labor, However, It did not go far enough

shorten：α-SMA and NKG2D are used as markers for activating HSC and NK cells, respectively. Immunofluorescence double staining technique was used to observe the expression of activated HSC and activated NK cells in liver tissue. In short, paraffin slices were baked, dewaxed with xylene, and dehydrated with gradient alcohol. Sections immersed in 0.01M citrate buffer (pH 6.0) were placed in a microwave oven for antigen retrieval for 20min. Then 0.2% TritonX-100 was added for permeation, 3% H2O2 deionized water to inactivate endogenous peroxidase, and 10% goat/donkey serum (selected according to secondary antibody) was incubated at 37℃ for 2h to block non-specific antibodies, followed by incubation with mixture of anti-α-SMA (1:300, Abcam, United Kingdom) and anti-NKG2D (1:300, Abcam, United Kingdom) primary antibodies at 4℃ for overnight. The slices were washed with TBST for three times and then incubated with secondary antibody Alexa Fluor 488 (Abcam, United Kingdom) and Alexa Fluor 594(Invitrogen, United States) at 37℃for 1h followed by DAPI for another 15min. The slices were observed using a DMI8 Leica Inverted fluorescence microscope.

The dimension of individualism-collectivism refers to “the degree to which a culture relies on and has allegiance to the self or the group” (Lustig & Koester, 2010, p.117). Cultures that rank low on individualism are highly collectivistic in nature and demand loyalty to the group. They believe that an individual’s primary obligations lie with the group, and they stress the dependence of individuals on organizations. On the other hand, in cultures that rank high on individualism, the autonomy of the individual is paramount and people are expected to take care of themselves. import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

def roberts_operator(I):
    M, N, _ = I.shape
    GX = 0
    GY = 0
    FI = 0
    T = 0
    for x in range(1, M - 1):
        for y in range(1, N - 1):
            GX = I[x - 1, y + 1] + 2 * I[x, y + 1] + I[x + 1, y + 1] - I[x - 1, y - 1] - 2 * I[x, y - 1] - I[
                x + 1, y - 1]
            GY = I[x + 1, y - 1] + 2 * I[x + 1, y] + I[x + 1, y + 1] - I[x - 1, y - 1] - 2 * I[x - 1, y] - I[
                x - 1, y + 1]
            SXY = np.sqrt(GX ** 2 + GY ** 2)
            if np.any(SXY > T):
                FI = FI + SXY ** 2
    return FI

def tenengrad_operator(I):
    M, N, _ = I.shape
    FI = 0
    for x in range(0, M - 2):
        for y in range(0, N):
            F1 = I[x + 2, y] - I[x, y]
            FI += F1 * F1
    return FI

We do not have to trust historians on these matters, for there are many parts of the world disadvantaged by local conditions where this is still the case. We can see them in the process of a transition towards the form of government we are used to, and we call it progress. Yet all such a transition does is change the scale of the problem: nations instead of villages. A scuffle between two mobs of villagers over whether the ziggurat should be blue or red has become a war between nations in which thousands lose their lives for reasons no less trivial or absurd. It's a surprise to me, Previously, I like many others thought 1937's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was the first feature-length animated film, but now I know the existence of Argentina animated feature-length El Apóstol made as early in 1917, That's 20 years earlier, Granted it used cutout animation not cel animation like Snow White did, I realize that it was not the first feature-length animated film

You know, I began to question how technically innovate Walt Disney truly was, Steamboat Willie wasn't the first sound cartoon, It was just an improvement over earlier sound cartoons like Inkwell Studios' Song Car-Tunes (1924–1926) and Van Beuren Studios' Dinner Time in that it featured a fully post-produced soundtrack and the Cinephone used in Steamboat Willie was really just a clone of the Phonofilm used in 16 Song Car-Tunes and while Disney was the first to use three-strip Technicolor in an animated film, they issued a pretty anti-competitive exclusivity deal preventing other animation studios like Fleischer Studios from using the process, but they didn't really invent the three-strip Technicolor process itself, that was by Technicolor, they were just the first to use it in animated film, when it comes to animation depth, they may have developed the multiplane camera in 1933 capturing parallax illusion but the Fleischers a year later developed a more sophisticated and superior device called the Stereoptical Camera that used three-dimensional miniature sets built to the scale of the animation artwork and the animation cels were placed within the setup so that various objects could pass in front of and behind them and the entire scene was shot using a horizontal camera and when it comes to Snow White, they were the first animated feature film to based on cel animation, but it wasn't the first animated feature film period as the existence of 1917's El Apóstol suggests

Amazon, Microsoft, and India crack down on tech support scams

Amazon, Microsoft, and India’s Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), the country’s federal enforcement agency, have announced a major crackdown on tech support fraud.

The CBI’s post details two instances where scammers pretended they were customer support agents for two “well-known multi-national companies” (Amazon and Microsoft) through pop-ups that “falsely appeared to be security alerts” from the companies.

Through their scheme, the scammers would get people to call a toll-free number to one of their call centers, take over a user’s computer remotely, convince users of the “pretense of non-existing problems,” and “make them pay hundreds of Dollars for unnecessary services” while impersonating as workers for Amazon and Microsoft.

Microsoft has a website detailing the popular versions of these scams, how to identify them, and steps on what to do if you believe you’ve been affected.

As part of the crackdown, “the CBI conducted intensive searches in five separate cases at 76 locations across multiple states,” the CBI wrote. “In the wake of Operation Chakra-II, 32 mobile phones, 48 laptops / hard disks, images of two servers, 33 SIM cards, and pen drives were confiscated and numerous bank accounts were freezed. CBI also seized a dump of 15 email accounts, illuminating the intricate web of deceit spun by the accused.”

“The illegal call centers impacted more than 2,000 Amazon and Microsoft customers primarily based in the US, but also in Australia, Canada, Germany, Spain, and the UK,” Amazon says in a blog post.

“This collaboration marks the first time Microsoft and Amazon have joined forces to combat tech support fraud,” Microsoft’s Amy Hogan-Burney writes in a blog post. “We firmly believe that partnerships like these are not only necessary but pivotal in creating a safer online ecosystem and in extending our protective reach to a larger number of individuals.”

Amazon has also poured extensive resources into combating counterfeit products on its store, announcing the Counterfeit Crimes Unit in 2020 to help lead the charge. And Microsoft fights online crime through its work with its Digital Crimes Unit.
